functions.name: ReleaseRenderTarget2D
functions.signature: ReleaseRenderTarget2D(Texture Render Target)
functions.docs:
Manually releases GPU resources of a render target. This is useful for blueprint creating a lot of render target that would
normally be released too late by the garbage collector that can be problematic on platforms that have tight GPU memory constrains.

functions.name: ResizeRenderTarget2D
functions.signature: ResizeRenderTarget2D(Texture Render Target, Width, Height)
functions.docs:
Changes the resolution of a render target. This is useful for when you need to resize the game viewport or change the in-game resolution during runtime
and thus need to update the sizes of all the render targets in the game accordingly.

functions.name: DrawMaterialToRenderTarget
functions.signature: DrawMaterialToRenderTarget(World Context Object, Texture Render Target, Material)
functions.docs:
Renders a quad with the material applied to the specified render target.
This sets the render target even if it is already set, which is an expensive operation.
Use BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget / EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget instead if rendering multiple primitives to the same render target.

functions.name: ExportRenderTarget

functions.docs: Exports a render target as a HDR or PNG image onto the disk (depending on the format of the render target)

functions.name: ReadRenderTargetPixel
functions.signature: ReadRenderTargetPixel(World Context Object, Texture Render Target, X, Y)
functions.docs:
Incredibly inefficient and slow operation! Read a value as sRGB color from a render target using integer pixel coordinates.
LDR render targets are assumed to be in sRGB space. HDR ones are assumed to be in linear space.
Result is 8-bit per channel [0,255] BGRA in sRGB space.

functions.name: ReadRenderTargetUV
functions.signature: ReadRenderTargetUV(World Context Object, Texture Render Target, U, V)
functions.docs:
Incredibly inefficient and slow operation! Read a value as sRGB color from a render target using UV [0,1]x[0,1] coordinates.
LDR render targets are assumed to be in sRGB space. HDR ones are assumed to be in linear space.
Result is 8-bit per channel [0,255] BGRA in sRGB space.

functions.name: ReadRenderTarget
functions.signature: ReadRenderTarget(World Context Object, Texture Render Target, Out Samples, Normalize)
functions.docs:
Incredibly inefficient and slow operation! Reads entire render target as sRGB color and returns a linear array of sRGB colors.
LDR render targets are assumed to be in sRGB space. HDR ones are assumed to be in linear space.
Result whether the operation succeeded.  If successful, OutSamples will an entry per pixel, where each is 8-bit per channel [0,255] BGRA in sRGB space.

functions.name: ReadRenderTargetRawPixel
functions.signature: ReadRenderTargetRawPixel(World Context Object, Texture Render Target, X, Y, Normalize)
functions.docs: Incredibly inefficient and slow operation! Read a value as-is from a render target using integer pixel coordinates.

functions.name: ReadRenderTargetRawPixelArea
functions.signature: ReadRenderTargetRawPixelArea(World Context Object, Texture Render Target, Min X, Min Y, Max X, Max Y, Normalize)
functions.docs: Incredibly inefficient and slow operation! Read an area of values as-is from a render target using a rectangle defined by integer pixel coordinates.

functions.name: ReadRenderTargetRawUV
functions.signature: ReadRenderTargetRawUV(World Context Object, Texture Render Target, U, V, Normalize)
functions.docs: Incredibly inefficient and slow operation! Read a value as-is from a render target using UV [0,1]x[0,1] coordinates.

functions.name: ReadRenderTargetRaw
functions.signature: ReadRenderTargetRaw(World Context Object, Texture Render Target, Out Linear Samples, Normalize)
functions.docs: Incredibly inefficient and slow operation! Read entire texture as-is from a render target.

functions.name: ReadRenderTargetRawUVArea
functions.signature: ReadRenderTargetRawUVArea(World Context Object, Texture Render Target, Area, Normalize)
functions.docs: Incredibly inefficient and slow operation! Read an area of values as-is from a render target using a rectangle defined by UV [0,1]x[0,1] coordinates.

functions.name: ImportBufferAsTexture2D

functions.docs: Imports a texture from a buffer and creates Texture2D from it.

functions.name: BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget
functions.signature: BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget(World Context Object, Texture Render Target, Canvas, Size, Context)
functions.docs:
Returns a Canvas object that can be used to draw to the specified render target.
Canvas has functions like DrawMaterial with size parameters that can be used to draw to a specific area of a render target.
Be sure to call EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget to complete the rendering!

functions.name: EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget
functions.signature: EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget(World Context Object, Context)
functions.docs: Must be paired with a BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget to complete rendering to a render target.

functions.name: SetCastInsetShadowForAllAttachments
functions.signature: SetCastInsetShadowForAllAttachments(Primitive Component, Cast Inset Shadow, Light Attachments As Group)
functions.docs:
Set the inset shadow casting state of the given component and all its child attachments.
Also choose if all attachments should be grouped for the inset shadow rendering. If enabled, one depth target will be shared for all attachments.

functions.name: CalculateProjectionMatrix
functions.signature: CalculateProjectionMatrix(Minimal View Info)
functions.docs: Calculates the projection matrix using this view info's aspect ratio (regardless of bConstrainAspectRatio)

functions.name: EnablePathTracing
functions.signature: EnablePathTracing(Enable Path Tracer)
functions.docs:
Enables or disables the path tracer for the current Game Viewport.
This command is equivalent to setting ShowFlag.PathTracing, but is accessible even from shipping builds.

functions.name: RefreshPathTracingOutput
functions.signature: RefreshPathTracingOutput()
functions.docs:
Forces the path tracer to restart sample accumulation.
This can be used to force the path tracer to compute a new frame in situations where it can not detect a change in the scene automatically.

functions.name: NumPrecompilingPSOsRemaining
functions.signature: NumPrecompilingPSOsRemaining()
functions.docs: Returns the number of active PSO precompilation tasks which are still running - can be used to extend loading screens to wait for PSO precaching to be finished
